 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 2285 of 2012  With  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 2286 of 2012  ==========================================================
 PATEL ASHOKBHAI HARIBHAI  Versus  MODI RAKESHKUMAR GORDHANDAS & ORS.

sentences.text: MR R.K.MANSURI(3205) for the Appellant(s) No. 1  MR DAKSHESH MEHTA(2430) for the Defendant(s) No. 5  MR. RUSHANG D MEHTA(6989) for the Defendant(s) No. 5  RULE SERVED for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2,4  SHARMISHTA A DAVE(8735) for the Defendant(s) No. 3
Date : 10/12/2024  COMMON ORAL ORDER 1.

Since both the First Appeals filed u/s 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short "the Act") arise out of selfsame accident having judgment and award in two different MACP being MACP Nos.1061 of 2001 and 1062 of 2001 filed u/s 166 of the Act and partly-allowing both the petitions by judgment and award dated 16.04.2010 passed by the learned MACT (Aux), Mahesana, they are being disposed of by this common order.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 The brief fact of the present appeal is such that on 27.04.2001 the claimant of M.A.C.P. No.1061 of 2001 was riding his motorcycle No.GJ2-P-6505 and claimant of M.A.C.P. No.1062 of 2001 was sitting as pillion rider on the said motorcycle and both Patel Ashokbhai Haribhai vs Modi Rakeshkumar Gordhandas on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123987649/
1 were going from Ranchhodpur to Vijapur.

entities.text: Patel Ashokbhai Haribhai vs Modi Rakeshkumar Gordhandas
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When they NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2285/2012 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined reached at the place of accident, one Jeep No.GJ-9-H-49 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the motorcycle.
As a result, the accident took place and the claimants sustained severe injuries.

The claimants have filed aforestated claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- and Rs.2,00,000/-
respectively.
The learned Tribunal vide impugned judgment and award dated 16.04.2010 has granted compensation to the tune of Rs.1,04,760/- and Rs.60,000/-, respectively.
Hence, the present appeal.

3. Heard learned advocate Mr.R.K.Mansuri appearing for the appellants - original claimants,
learned advocate Ms.Sharmishta Dave appearing for the United Indian Insurance Company Limited and learned advocate Mr.Rushang Mehta appearing for the Oriental Insurance Company Limited.
4.
In the matter on hand, the Oriental Insurance Company Limited has purchased the risk of driver of bullet motorcycle, whereas United India Insurance Company Limited has purchased the risk of Jeep.
Both vehicles are involved in the road accident.

5. The sum and substance of the argument of learned advocate Mr.Mansuri is to the extent that the road accident took place between bullet and jeep on the highway from Ranchhodpur to Vijapur whereby the bullet was ridden by Ashokkumar Haribhai and Kanubhai Shankarbhai was sitting as pillion rider in the bullet motorcycle.

He would further submit that the accident took place as head on collision between bullet and jeep NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2285/2012 ORDER DATED:
10/12/2024 undefined coming from the other side.

Learned advocate Mr.Mansuri would further submit that learned Tribunal has assessed inter se negligence / contributory negligence of drivers of both the offending vehicle in tune of 40% to the bullet driver and 60% to the jeep driver.
He would submit that he is not questioning such finding of learned Tribunal.
He would submit that learned Tribunal has committed two errors.

First of all, the learned Tribunal failed to read Exhibit-32, the licence of the jeep driver whereby he has authorized to driver LMV but yet learned Tribunal believed that he is authorized to drive auto rickshaw only and exonerated the Insurance Company.

Therefore,
he submits that error in perusing the evidence committed by the learned Tribunal should be rectified by this Court by allowing this appeal.
6. As far as income of the claimants are concerned, he would submit that learned Tribunal has taken income on lower side and not granted the compensation for loss of future prospects.
Therefore, he submits to allow the appeal and to recalculate the compensation.
7. Learned advocate Ms.Sharmishta Dave for the United India Insurance Company Limited supports the impugned judgment and award and submits to pass necessary orders.

8. Learned advocate Mr.Rushang Mehta submits that he has been exonerated as far as M.A.C.P.
No.1061 of 2001 is concerned as the claimant himself was the driver of the bullet and he cannot take Patel Ashokbhai Haribhai vs Modi Rakeshkumar Gordhandas on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123987649/
2 compensation from his own Insurance Company.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as second M.A.C.P. is concerned, he submits to pass necessary orders.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2285/2012 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined 9.

In wake of the above reasons, while appreciating evidence on record, what could be noticeable that in Exhibit-32, RTO has specifically endorsed that the driver of the jeep has passed the LMV test on 23.06.1999 and was authorized to driver LMV.
The road accident took place on 27.04.2001 which demonstrates that driver of the jeep was authorized to drive the jeep on that day.
Learned Tribunal has misread Exhibit-32 and committed serious error in exonerating Insurance Company.

According to this Court, since driver of jeep was authorized to drive LMV, even as per the RTO endorsement on the date of accident, the Insurance Company cannot claim breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The Insurance Company is, therefore, legitimately bound to indemnify the risk of the owner in absence of any other defense.
Therefore, the United India Insurance Company Limited is fastened with liability to pay the compensation.
10. Perusing the impugned judgment and award, it appears that learned Tribunal has taken up conservative view to assess the compensation.

For calculating the future loss of income, the amount of Rs.2,000/- has been taken by the learned Tribunal, but looking to the fact that the claimants are engaged in the business and taking the time period of road accident being 2001 and also keeping in mind rate of minimum wage, I think that Rs.2,500/- per month would be the relevant and proper income to decide the compensation for loss of future prospects.

40% prospective income is required to be granted for computing loss of future prospects as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi - 2017 (16) SCC 680.

Therefore, I hold that the claimant in First Appeal No.2285 of 2012 is entitled to get the entire decretal amount of compensation of Rs.90,420/- with 7.5% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realization and claimant in First Appeal No.2286 of 2012 is entitled to get the entire decretal amount of compensation of Rs.97,200/- with 7.5% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realization, which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
12. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
12.1 The present appeals are partly allowed.
12.2 In First Appeal No.2285 of 2012, opponent Nos.1 to 3 of the M.A.C.P. No.1061 of 2001 are liable to pay the compensation as stated hereinabove to the claimants jointly and severally.

Insurance Companies are directed to deposit the entire decretal amount with interest as stated hereinabove Patel Ashokbhai Haribhai vs Modi Rakeshkumar Gordhandas on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123987649/
4 before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
